rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar is reported to have wiped only the fontanelle when wiping the head.
rows.anchor: فروي عن ابن عمر: أنه مسح اليافوخ فقط،

rows.speaker: سلمة بن الأكوع
rows.claim: Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ is reported to have wiped the front of his head.
rows.anchor: وعن سلمة بن الأكوع أنه كان يمسح مقدم رأسه،

rows.speaker: إبراهيم والشعبي
rows.claim: Ibrahim and al-Shaʿbi hold that wiping any part of the head suffices.
rows.anchor: وعن إبراهيم والشعبي: أي نواحي رأسك مسحت أجزأك،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says that a woman who can reach only one hair with her wipe has fulfilled the requirement.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن: إن لم تصب المرأة إلا شعرة واحدة أجزأها.

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: The well-known Maliki position requires wiping the whole head.
rows.anchor: فالمشهور من مذهب مالك: وجوب التعميم.

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: The well-known Shafiʿi position requires the smallest amount that can be called wiping.
rows.anchor: والمشهور من مذهب الشافعي: وجوب أدنى ما ينطلق عليه اسم المسح،

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة والشافعي
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and al-Shafiʿi regard wiping the whole head as preferable.
rows.anchor: ومشهور أبي حنيفة والشافعي: أن الأفضل استيعاب الجميع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the analogy that the head is merely an instrument for wiping the hand: applying that logic to tayammum would imply wiping only parts of the face and hands.
rows.anchor: فكما أنه لا يدل هذا على تعميم جميع اليد بجزء من أجزاء المنديل فكذلك الآية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One washing or wiping fulfills the command; repeating washing three times is sunnah.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الأمر بالغسل والمسح يقع الامتثال فيه بمرة واحدة، وتثليث المعسول سنة.

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومالك
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and Malik do not regard repeating the washing three times as sunnah.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة ومالك: ليس بسنة.

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi holds that wiping is repeated three times; the same is reported from Anas, Ibn Jubayr, and ʿAta.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: بتثليث المسح. وروي عن أنس، وابن جبير، وعطاء مثله.

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin is reported to have wiped twice.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن سيرين: يمسح مرتين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's apparent meaning is that whichever way one wipes, it suffices.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من الآية: أنه كيفما مسح أجزأه.

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأحمد وجماعة من الصحابة والتابعين
rows.claim: The sound Sunnah establishes beginning at the front, wiping toward the nape, then returning toward the middle; these authorities follow this direction.
rows.anchor: الثابت منها في السنة الصحيحة الأول، وهو قول: مالك، والشافعي، وأحمد، وجماعة من الصحابة والتابعين.

rows.speaker: الحسن بن حي
rows.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Hayy holds the second of the three reported preferred directions for wiping the head.
rows.anchor: والثاني: منها قول الحسن بن حي. والثالث: عن ابن عمر.

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar holds the third of the reported preferred directions for wiping the head.
rows.anchor: والثاني: منها قول الحسن بن حي. والثالث: عن ابن عمر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning the hands over the hair after the initial wipe is not obligatory; the wipe is complete without returning them.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن رد اليدين على شعر الرأس ليس بفرض، فتحقق المسح بدون الرد.

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some authorities hold that returning the hands over the head is obligatory.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن رد اليدين على شعر الرأس ليس بفرض، فتحقق المسح بدون الرد. وقال بعضهم: هو فرض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wiping over a turban does not suffice because it is not a wipe of the head itself.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المسح على العمامة لا يجزئ لأنه ليس مسحا للرأس.

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي والثوري وأحمد
rows.claim: Al-Awzaʿi, al-Thawri, and Ahmad hold that wiping over a turban suffices and that even one finger suffices for the wipe.
rows.anchor: وقال الأوزاعي، والثوري، وأحمد: يجزئ، وأن المسح يجزئ ولو بأصبع واحدة.

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأبو يوسف ومحمد
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad hold that at least three fingers are needed for the wipe.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وأبو يوسف ومحمد: لا يجزئ بأقل من ثلاث أصابع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent command does not permit replacing the prescribed wipe with washing the head; this is also attributed to Ibn al-Qadi and follows the Zahiri position.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه لو غسل رأسه لم يجزه، لأن الغسل ليس هو المأمور به

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi knows of no disagreement that washing suffices for wiping, except a report from al-Shashi that Ibn al-Qadi said it does not.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن العربي: لا نعلم خلافا في أن الغسل يجزيه من المسح إلا ما روى لنا الشاشي

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو بكر
rows.claim: These reciters, also followed in reports by Anas, ʿIkrima, al-Shaʿbi, al-Baqir, Qatada, ʿAlqama, and al-Dahhak, read the feet in the genitive, whose apparent syntax includes them in wiping with the head.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو بكر، وهي قراءة أنس، وعكرمة، والشعبي،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأنس وعكرمة والشعبي وأبو جعفر الباقر
rows.claim: Wiping the feet is reported as obligatory from these authorities and is the Imami Shia position.
rows.anchor: وروي وجوب مسح الرجلين عن. ابن عباس، وأنس، وعكرمة، والشعبي، وأبي جعفر الباقر

rows.speaker: جمهور الفقهاء
rows.claim: The majority of jurists hold that washing the feet is obligatory.
rows.anchor: وقال جمهور الفقهاء: فرضهما الغسل.

rows.speaker: داود والناصر للحق
rows.claim: Dawud and al-Nasir li-l-Haqq require combining wiping and washing the feet.
rows.anchor: وقال داود: يجب الجمع بين المسح والغسل، وهو قول الناصر للحق

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري وابن جرير الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari allow a choice between wiping and washing the feet.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري، وابن جرير الطبري: يخير بين المسح والغسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls the washing camp's syntactic interpretations of the genitive far-fetched and condemns its economy-of-water reading as contrived and obscure.
rows.anchor: وهو كما ترى في غاية التلفيق وتعمية في الأحكام.

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd says Arabs call light washing wiping, as in saying they wiped themselves for prayer to mean they washed their limbs.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي زيد: أن العرب تسمي الغسل الخفيف مسحا ويقولون: تمسحت للصلاة

rows.speaker: نافع والكسائي وابن عامر وحفص
rows.claim: Nafiʿ, al-Kisaʾi, Ibn ʿAmir, and Hafs read “the feet” in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع، والكسائي، وابن عامر، وحفص: وأرجلكم بالنصب.

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ allows parsing the accusative feet as coordinated with faces and hands, despite the intervening clause.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: هذا جائز بلا خلاف.

rows.speaker: الأستاذ أبو الحسن بن عصفور
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAsfur says separating a coordinate from its antecedent is especially ugly when the intervening material is a clause, suggesting this parse should be avoided for the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قال الأستاذ أبو الحسن بن عصفور: وقد ذكر الفصل بين المعطوف والمعطوف عليه، قال: وأقبح ما يكون ذلك بالجمل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative coordination with faces and hands represents the view that washing the feet is required; those who require wiping coordinate the word with the syntactic position of “your heads.”
rows.anchor: وهذا تخريج من يرى أن فرض الرجلين هو الغسل، وأما من يرى المسح فيجعله معطوفا على موضع برؤوسكم،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads the feet in the nominative, with an omitted predicate meaning either “wash them” or “wipe them,” according to the legal position adopted.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: وأرجلكم بالرفع، وهو مبتدأ محذوف الخبر أي: اغسلوها إلى الكعبين

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says, to his knowledge, the majority agree that the ankle bones mark the ablution limit, and no one places it at the bone on the top of the foot.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: قول الجمهور هما حد الوضوء بإجماع فيما علمت، ولا أعلم أحدا جعل حد الوضوء

rows.speaker: الإمامية
rows.claim: The Imamis say those requiring wiping to the ankle use the ankle bone on the top of the foot as the endpoint.
rows.anchor: قالت الإمامية: وكل من ذهب إلى وجوب مسح الكعب هو الذي في وجه القدم،

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya transmits from Ashhab from Malik that the ankles are the two bones joined to the shin and aligned with the heel, not the visible bone atop the foot; he draws an analogy with the singular elbow in each hand.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: روى أشهب عن مالك: الكعبان هما العظمان الملتصغان بالساق المحاذيان للعقب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not establish uninterrupted performance as a condition for valid ablution; the well-known Hanafi and Maliki position does not require continuity, though an older report from Malik and al-Shafiʿi makes it a condition.
rows.anchor: ولا دليل في قوله في الآية على أن موالاة أفعال الوضوء ليست بشرط في صحته لقبول الآية

rows.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Malik and Abu Hanifa do not require the ablution actions to follow a particular order because the verse coordinates them with waw.
rows.anchor: وعلى أن الترتيب في الأفعال ليس بشرط لعطفها بالواو وهو مذهب مالك وأبي حنيفة،

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi requires the ablution actions to be performed in the stated order.
rows.anchor: ومذهب الشافعي أنه شرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not explicitly address the ears; positions about their status determine whether they are wiped, washed, or treated as independent.
rows.anchor: ولم تتعرض الآية للنص على الأذنين.

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه والثوري والأوزاعي ومالك
rows.claim: These authorities treat the ears as part of the head and wipe them, according to a report from Malik via Ashhab and Ibn al-Qasim.
rows.anchor: فمذهب أبي حنيفة وأصحابه والثوري، والأوزاعي، ومالك فيما روى عنه أشهب وابن القاسم:

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri regards the ears as part of the face and washes them with it.
rows.anchor: وقال الزهري: هما من الوجه فيغسلان معه.

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi treats the ears as an independent organ, neither face nor head, and wipes them with fresh water.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: من الوجه هما عضو قائم بنفسه، ليسا من الوجه ولا من الرأس،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view assigns the front of the ears to the face and the rear to the head, with their washing or wiping status following that division.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما أقبل منهما من الوجه وما أدبر من الرأس،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning minor purification, the author says the verse moves to major purification and recalls the earlier meaning of “junub.”
rows.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى الطهارة الصغرى ذكر الطهارة الكبرى، وتقدم مدلول الجنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent command is that a person in a state of major impurity must perform a full bath.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الجنب مأمور بالاغتسال.

rows.speaker: عمر وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Umar and Ibn Masʿud said a person in major impurity cannot perform tayammum and must leave prayer until finding water; the majority disagreed, and the two later returned to the majority position.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر، وابن مسعود: لا يتيمم الجنب البتة، بل يدع الصلاة حتى يجد الماء، والجمهور على خلاف ذلك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is that washing, wiping, and purification use water; the move from water to clean earth in tayammum leaves no intermediary, as the majority hold.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الغسل والمسح والتطهر إنما تكون بالماء لقوله: فلم تجدوا ماء

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي والأصم
rows.claim: Al-Awzaʿi and al-Asamm allow ablution and bathing with any pure liquid.
rows.anchor: وذهب الأوزاعي والأصم: إلى أنه يجوز الوضوء والغسل بجميع المائعات الطاهرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning does not require a separate ablution for a person performing the major purification bath.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الجنب لا يجب عليه غير التطهير من غير وضوء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obligatory bath requires water to reach the entire body, without a prescribed order among washed parts, rubbing, mouth rinsing, or nasal rinsing.
rows.anchor: ولا ترتيب في الأعضاء المغسولة، ولا دلك، ولا مضمضة، ولا استنشاق، بل الواجب تعميم جسده

rows.speaker: داود وأبو ثور
rows.claim: Dawud and Abu Thawr require doing ablution before the full bath.
rows.anchor: وقال داود وأبو ثور: يجب تقديم الوضوء على الغسل.

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd glosses al-maʾfuk as foolish or weak-minded.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: المأفوك المأفون، وهو الضعيف العقل.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda says a maʾfuk man fails to attain good; a town being overturned yields the name for the overturned cities of Lot, and al-muʾtafikāt can refer to winds with varying directions.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: رجل مأفوك لا يصيب خيرا، وائتفكت البلدة بأهلها انقلبت،

rows.speaker: الزهري وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri and others report that the verse was revealed over a long story involving ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubay retaining his Jewish alliance and ʿUbada ibn al-Samit repudiating such an alliance after Badr; the author gives a summary.
rows.anchor: قال الزهري وغيره: سبب نزولها ولها قصة عبد الله بن أبي واستمساكه بحلف يهود،

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says the occasion was Abu Lubaba ibn ʿAbd al-Mundhir signalling to Qurayza that they would be slaughtered when they asked his opinion about submitting to Saʿd ibn Muʿadh's judgment.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: سببها أمر أبي لبابة بن عبد المنذر وإشارته إلى قريظة أنه الذبح

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says that after the Muslims' setback at Uhud, some proposed seeking a Jewish pact for aid against Quraysh or the Arabs, while others proposed joining the Christians, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: لما نزل بالمسلمين أمر أحد فزع منهم قوم، وقال بعضهم لبعض: نأخذ من اليهود عهدا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account takes the verse generally as concerning hypocrites who outwardly professed faith while supporting Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي عامة في المنافقين أظهروا الإيمان وظاهروا اليهود والنصارى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition means believers must not support Jews or Christians, seek their support, or socialize with them as fellow believers.
rows.anchor: نهى تعالى المؤمنين عن موالاة اليهود والنصارى ينصرونهم ويستنصرون بهم،

rows.speaker: أبي وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ubay and Ibn ʿAbbas are reported to read “arbāban” in place of “awliyāʾ.”
rows.anchor: وقراءة أبي وابن عباس: أربابا مكان أولياء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause that some are allies of others indicates the cause of the alliance: their shared unbelief and collusion against believers.
rows.anchor: بعضهم أولياء بعض جملة معطوفة من النهي مشعرة بعلة الولاية وهو اجتماعهم في الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent referent of “some of them” is the Jews and Christians together.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في بعضهم يعود على اليهود والنصارى.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One alternative supplies an ellipsis: some Jews ally with other Jews and some Christians with other Christians, since the two groups are not allies to one another.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى على أن ثم محذوفا والتقدير: بعض اليهود أولياء بعض،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says the collective pronoun generalizes their groups, while their mutual enmity shows that each group affiliates only with its own kind.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يقال: جمعهم في الضمير على سبيل الإجمال، ودل ما بينهم من المعاداة على التفصيل،

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Hawfi parses “some of them are allies of others” as a nominal clause functioning adjectivally for “allies.”
rows.anchor: قال الحوفي: هي جملة من مبتدأ وخبر في موضع النعت لأولياء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers treating that clause as an independent sentence with no syntactic position.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنها جملة مستأنفة لا موضع لها من الإعراب.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the warning means that whoever allies with them in religion is one of them in unbelief.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فإنه منهم في حكم الكفر، أي ومن يتولهم في الدين.

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another authority says that whoever allies with them in worldly life will be one of them in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: ومن يتولهم في الدنيا فإنه منهم في الآخرة.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says that whoever allies with them by covenant shares in violating the command.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ومن يتولهم منكم في العهد فإنه منهم في مخالفة الأمر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is a severe warning to disavow unbelievers and abandon their alliance, directed at ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubay and those like him.
rows.anchor: وهذا تشديد عظيم في الانتفاء من أهل الكفر، وترك موالاتهم، وإنحاء عبد الله بن أبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mere dealings without sincere friendship do not count as alliance; acting in their favor without adopting their belief brings blame, whereas alliance in belief amounts to unbelief.
rows.anchor: ولا يدخل في الموالاة لليهود والنصارى من غير مصافاة، ومن تولاهم بأفعاله دون معتقده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and others use the verse to permit eating slaughtered animals of Arab Christians, reasoning that a person who enters a people's religion is one of them.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل بهذا ابن عباس وغيره على جواز أكل ذبائح نصارى العرب،

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: When asked about a man selling his house to a Christian to use as a church, Ibn Sirin recited this verse.
rows.anchor: وسئل ابن سيرين عن رجل يبيع داره لنصراني ليتخذها كنيسة: فتلا هذه الآية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith warns that the two fires should not be visible to each other, in the context of separation from unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث: «لا تراءى ناراهما»

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar told Abu Musa not to honor, trust, or draw near his Christian clerk because God had humiliated, deemed untrustworthy, and excluded Christians; Abu Musa said the treasury depended on him, and Umar dismissed the matter.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر لأبي موسى في كاتبه النصراني: لا تكرموهم إذ أهانهم الله، ولا تأمنوهم إذ خونهم الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's general wording is particular in sense: God does not guide those He has foreknown will not be guided.
rows.anchor: إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين ظاهره العموم والمعنى على الخصوص،

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya limits the statement to the period when a person is engaged in wrongdoing, since wrongdoing contains no guidance and the wrongdoer is not guided in that act.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: أو يراد التخصيص مدة الظلم والتلبس بفعله،

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya defines the wrongdoer as one who refuses to say that God alone deserves worship and has no partner.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: الظالم من أبى أن يقول لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له.

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the wrongdoers meant here are the hypocrites.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: أراد المنافقين. وقيل:

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation identifies the wrongdoer as someone who places alliance in the wrong place.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الظالم هو الذي وضع الولاية في غير موضعها.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says those who wrong themselves by allying with unbelief are denied God's grace and abandoned as punishment; the author notes this is a Muʿtazili approach.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري قريبا من هذا، قال: يعني الذين ظلموا أنفسهم بموالاة الكفر يمنعهم الله ألطافه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to the Messenger; those whose hearts are diseased are ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubay and his hypocrite followers, or Khazraj believers who followed from ignorance and partisanship, as Ibn ʿAtiyya says.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، والذين في قلوبهم مرض عبد الله بن أبي ومن تبعه من المنافقين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their rushing among the Jews means hastening toward alliance with them and desiring it.
rows.anchor: ومعنى يسارعون فيهم: أي في موالاتهم ويرغبون فيها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author points back to the discussion of heart disease at the beginning of al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وتقدم الكلام في المرض في أول البقرة.

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن وثاب
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn Waththab reads “fa-yara” with a third-person yaʾ; its subject is either God or opinion/reason.
rows.anchor: وقرأ إبراهيم بن وثاب: فيرى بالياء من تحت، والفاعل ضمير يعود على الله، أو الرأي.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya suggests “those” could be the subject of “you see,” with the meaning that they hasten and an implied “an” omitted for brevity.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويحتمل أن يكون الذين فاعل ترى، والمعنى: أن يسارعوا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Ibn ʿAtiyya's proposed omission of “an” because such deletion is not a regular construction.
rows.anchor: وهذا ضعيف لأن حذف إن من نحو هذا لا ينقاس.

rows.speaker: قتادة والأعمش
rows.claim: Qatada and al-Aʿmash read “yusriʿun,” without the alif, from the form meaning “they hasten.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة والأعمش: يسرعون بغير ألف من أسرع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If “you see” means sight, “they hasten” is circumstantial; if it means cognition, the phrase is its second object.
rows.anchor: فترى إن كانت من رؤية العين كان يسارعون حالا، أو من رؤية القلب ففي موضع المفعول الثاني،

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي
rows.claim: The statement “we fear an adverse turn” is preserved from ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubay, and many hypocrites said it with him.
rows.anchor: هذا محفوظ من قول عبد الله بن أبي، وقاله معه منافقون كثيرون.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains their fear as concern that Muhammad's cause would not succeed and that power might turn against them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: معناه نخشى أن لا يتم أمر محمد فيدور الأمر علينا.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation takes the feared adverse turn to mean drought and famine.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الدائرة من جدب وقحط.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says they feared that the Jews would stop supplying or lending to them.
rows.anchor: ولا يميروننا ولا يقرضوننا.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says circumstances might force them to rely on the Jews for assistance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: دائرة تحوج إلى يهود وإلى معونتهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that God may bring victory or another intervention is good news to the Messenger and believers that God will grant victory and aid.
rows.anchor: هذا بشارة للرسول والمؤمنين بوعده تعالى بالفتح والنصرة.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says “the opening” means God's judgment in these events, and al-Fattah means judge.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: عنى به القضاء في هذه النوازل والفتاح الفاضي.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi interprets the promised opening as the conquest of Mecca.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: يعني به فتح مكة.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the apparent meaning is the Messenger's triumph and elevation of his cause, leaving no need for the Jews.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وظاهر الفتح في هذه الآية ظهور رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the opening as conquest of the lands of the polytheists.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فتح بلاد المشركين.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes it as conquest of Jewish settlements such as Qurayza, al-Nadir, and Fadak.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فتح قرى اليهود، يريدون قريظة والنضير وفدك

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses “opening” as relief.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الفتح الفرج، قاله ابن قتيبة.

rows.speaker: ابن السائب ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn al-Saʾib and Muqatil interpret “an affair from Him” as the expulsion and confiscation of Banu al-Nadir without human action because God cast terror into them; it also encompasses Qurayza's killing and capture of their children.
rows.anchor: لم يكن للناس فيه فعل بل طرح الله في قلوبهم الرعب فأعطوا بأيديهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says the Jews would be humiliated until they paid the jizya.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إذلالهم حتى يعطوا الجزية.

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba interprets the promised affair as fertility and prosperity.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الخصب والرخاء قاله ابن قتيبة.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says it means God will expose the hypocrites and their anticipation of misfortune.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: إظهار أمر المنافقين وتربصهم الدوائر.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the alternatives distinguish an opening brought about through the Prophet and companions' efforts from divine intervention that destroys the enemies of the religion without human causation.
rows.anchor: فوعد الله تعالى إما بفتح يقتضي تلك الأعمال، وإما بأمر من عنده يهلك أعداء الشرع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites will regret having thought the Prophet's cause would fail and that power would not belong to the believers.
rows.anchor: أي يصيرون نادمين على ما حدثتهم أنفسهم أن أمر النبي لا يتم،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes what they concealed to be their alliance with the Jews.
rows.anchor: وقيل: موالاتهم.

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reads “fa-tusbih al-fussaq,” explicitly substituting “the wicked” for the pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير: فتصبح الفساق جعل الفساق مكان الضمير.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says morning is singled out because people think at night and see the result of those thoughts in the morning.
rows.anchor: قال بن عطية: وخص الإصباح بالذكر لأن الإنسان في ليله مفكر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb “asbaha” can mean “became” without specifying that the change occurred in the morning.
rows.anchor: وذكرنا أن أصبح تأتي بمعنى صار من غير اعتبار كينونة في الصباح،

rows.speaker: الحوفي وأبو البقاء
rows.claim: Al-Hawfi and Abu al-Baqaʾ coordinate “fa-yusbihu” with “an yaʾti”; the causal sense of fa permits this, while coordination without it would require a missing link to God's predicate.
rows.anchor: واتفق الحوفي وأبو البقاء على أن قوله: فيصبحوا معطوف على قوله: أن يأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa is the only coordinating particle that can license one pronoun to serve in two clauses, as in relative clauses, descriptions, or predicates.
rows.anchor: لكن الفاء انفردت من بين سائر حروف العطف بتسويغ الاكتفاء بضمير واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “fa-yusbihu” may be subjunctive after an implicit “an” in the response to “asa” understood as human wishing; the author questions whether hopeful “asa” works like “layta.”
rows.anchor: وجوز أن لا يكون معطوفا على أن يأتي، ولكنه منصوب بإضمار أن بعد الفاء في جواب التمني،

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators say hypocrites mourned the expulsion of Banu al-Nadir and, after Qurayza was killed, openly voiced their hidden loyalty to the Jews; believers were astonished that those who swore to support them had colluded with the Jews.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: لما أجلى بني النضير تأسف المنافقون على فراقهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second possible audience is the Jews: believers address them because hypocrites had sworn to aid them, as in the pledge described in 59:11.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يقول المؤمنون ذلك لليهود، ويكون الخطاب في قوله: إنهم لمعكم لليهود،

rows.speaker: الابنان ونافع
rows.claim: The two sons and Nafiʿ read without the waw, as though answering what believers say; this reading appears in Meccan and Medinan codices.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الابنان ونافع: بغير واو، كأنه جواب قائل ما يقول المؤمنون حينئذ.

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers retain the waw; Abu ʿAmr reads the lām with fatḥa and the Kufans with ḍamma; ʿAli ibn Nasr transmits both from Abu ʿAmr.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: بالواو، ونصب اللام أبو عمرو، ورفعها الكوفيون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the waw and nominative reading, the sentence is coordinated to another sentence; without waw, its connection remains clear through repeated reference to those who rushed to the Jews and feared a reversal.
rows.anchor: والواو عاطفة جملة على جملة، هذا إذا رفع اللام، ومع حذف الواو الاتصال موجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading places the believers' statement at the time of victory.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا القول هو صادر من المؤمنين عند رؤية الفتح كما قدمنا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible setting is the affair of Banu Qaynuqaʿ, when ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubay sought their release and claimed his fear concerned the city and its believers, though believers knew he was lying.
rows.anchor: قيل: ويحتمل أن يكون في وقت الذين في قلوبهم مرض يقولون: نخشى أن تصيبنا دائرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative reading “wa-yaqula” may coordinate by meaning with “an yaʾti”; the author lists other parses involving an omitted pronoun, apposition, or coordination to “fa-yusbihu.”
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة ويقول بالنصب، فوجهت على أن هذا القول لم يكن إلا عند الفتح،

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ allows an omitted pronoun meaning “by Him,” or treats the infinitive phrase as apposition to God's name so that “asa” is complete, or coordinates it with “fa-yusbihu.”
rows.anchor: وأجاز ذلك أبو البقاء على تقدير ضمير محذوف أي: ويقول الذين آمنوا به، أي بالله.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية عن أبي يعلى وابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya, citing Abu Yaʿla, and Ibn al-Hajib allow coordination as “may God and the believers say”; the author says this works only with an implied link to their support of God's religion.
rows.anchor: وذكر هذا الوجه ابن عطية عن أبي يعلى، وتبعه ابن الحاجب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hope is impossible for God because what He promises is certain; the proposed hopeful parsing is therefore questioned.
rows.anchor: وعسى من الله واجبة فلا ترجي فيها،

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas proposes another coordination for the accusative reading, which the author takes up and refutes in the following segment.
rows.anchor: وخرجه النحاس على أن يكون معطوفا على قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Nahhas's coordination: it separates coordinated elements with “or an affair from Him,” treats “opening” as a verbal noun without warrant, gives the wrong sense, and leaves “fa-yusbihu” as an intervening clause.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح هذا لأنه قد فصل بينهما بقوله: أو أمر من عنده،

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya questions the ban on saying “may God and the believers say,” since those supported by God say they will support him by manifesting his religion.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: عندي في منع جواز عسى الله أن يقول المؤمنون نظر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This coordination works only if an implicit link to God's support and manifestation of His religion is supplied; the objection applies only when no such link exists.
rows.anchor: وإنما منعوا حيث لا يكون رابط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Jahd” is an emphatic verbal noun: the hypocrites swore with great effort that they were with the believers, then their alliance with the Jews exposed the falsehood.
rows.anchor: وانتصاب جهد على أنه مصدر مؤكد، والمعنى: أهؤلاء هم المقسمون باجتهاد منهم في الأيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Jahd” may also be parsed as a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن ينتصب على الحال، كما جوزوا في فعلته جهدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They are with you” conveys the meaning of the oath, not its exact wording; the literal wording would be “we are with you.”
rows.anchor: وقوله: إنهم لمعكم، حكاية لمعنى القسم لا للفظهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading makes “their deeds were void” part of the believers' statement, though it could instead be God's report or a supplication by God or the believers.
rows.anchor: ظاهره أنه من جملة ما يقوله المؤمنون اعتمادا في الإخبار على ما حصل في اعتقادهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari hears an exclamation: how void their deeds were and how great their loss.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وفيه معنى التعجب كأنه قيل: ما أحبط أعمالهم فما أخسرهم!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The voiding of deeds is figurative, since hypocrites have no genuine deeds to be nullified in reality.
rows.anchor: وحبط العمل هنا هو على معنى التشبيه، وإلا فلا عمل له في الحقيقة

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Hawfi parses “their deeds were void” either as a second predicate of “those,” or as a relative clause describing them with the voiding statement as its predicate.
rows.anchor: وجوز الحوفي أن يكون حبطت أعمالهم خبرا ثانيا عن هؤلاء،

rows.speaker: أبو واقد والجراح
rows.claim: Abu Waqid and al-Jarrah read “habitat” with fatḥa on the bāʾ, a dialectal form.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم ذكر قراءة أبي واقد والجراح حبطت بفتح الباء وأنها لغة.
